c: A subprogram groups reusable instructions. A function can be called with different arguments, executes its instructions and returns a result.
An array parameter allows one function to accept an array argument, rather than a separate parameter for each element. For example, values[0] reads the first supplied element.
RETURN sends a function result to the caller. When firstValue([6,3,8]) returns the element at index 0, the caller receives 6.
Test array functions on several arrays, including different lengths. If a one-element array is supplied, code reading element [1] must reject it or handle it safely.

m.title: Worked trace · array parameter
m.q: A function firstValue(values) returns values[0]. The caller passes scores = [6,3,8] and prints firstValue(scores). Trace the parameter and return. [4 marks]
st: scores is passed as the array argument to the parameter values. [1]
values[0] is the first element of [6,3,8], which is 6. [1]
RETURN sends 6 back to the function call. [1]
PRINT outputs 6. The same function can be reused for other arrays. [1]

w: A function lastValue(items) returns items[2]. What does it return for stock = [8,3,5], and why? [2 marks]
5 [1]; index 2 means the third element when indexing starts at 0 [1].
A function firstScore(results) returns results[0]. What does it return for [7,4,9] and [2,6,8]? [2 marks]
7 for the first array [1] and 2 for the second [1].
A function adds elements at indices 0 and 1. Predict outputs for arrays [4,6] and [0,0]. Explain why array [9] needs special handling. [4 marks]
[4,6] returns 10 [1]; [0,0] returns 0 [1]; [9] has no index 1 [1], so check the length or require two elements before indexing [1].
wSteps: Use the same function with each argument.
Check the length or enforce an array of at least two items [1].

k.q: Trace this OCR ERL program; predict the output and change it.
k.code:
function firstValue(values)
    return values[0]
endfunction
array scores = [6,3,8]
print(firstValue(scores))
p: Change scores[0] to 9 before the function call.
Add print(scores[1]) after the function call.
k.a:
Original output: 6.
After the changes: Changed first element prints 9; scores[1] prints 3.
